feedback.problem:
Let $V={R}^{3}$ be the vector space equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x,y⟩=2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+5{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{3}{y}_{3}.
$$

If $x=[\begin{aligned}k \\ -3 \\ 4\end{aligned}]$ and $y=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]$ are orthogonal with respect to the inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ in $V,$ then $k=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since $x$ and $y$ are orthogonal, their inner product must be zero.

First, we compute the inner product using our definition:

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =2{x}_{1}{y}_{1}+5{x}_{2}{y}_{2}+3{x}_{3}{y}_{3} \\  & =2(k\cdot (-3))+5\cdot (-3\cdot 2)+3\cdot (4\cdot 3) \\  & =-6k-30+36 \\  & =6-6k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set $⟨x,y⟩=0$ and solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y⟩ & =0 \\ 6-6k & =0 \\ 6k & =6 \\ k & =1\end{aligned}
$$
